variants.title: Melting point of ice
variants.sample: Ice and water in the beaker
variants.method: warm a beaker of crushed ice gently and follow the thermometer
variants.unknown: the temperature at which ice melts
variants.note: 100 g of ice needs 33.4 kJ to melt. While it melts, the mixture holds at 0 °C however gently it is warmed.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, enthalpy of fusion of water (334 kJ/kg at 0 °C, 101.325 kPa)

variants.title: Boiling point of water on a high hill
variants.sample: Water at a pressure of 80 kPa
variants.method: boil water where the air pressure is lower, about 2,000 m above sea level
variants.unknown: the temperature at which water boils under 80 kPa
variants.note: Water boils when its vapour pressure equals the pressure above it, so lower pressure means a lower boiling point: 93.5 °C at 80 kPa instead of 100 °C at sea level.

source.title: Steam tables (IAPWS-IF97): saturation temperature of water at 80 kPa is 93.5 °C
